target: Skorstensfejarens uniform var svart av sot och aska.
english: The chimney sweep's uniform was black from soot and ash.
tip: Swedish stacks words into long compounds: skorstensfejarens builds from skorsten (chimney) and fejare (sweeper). The last part sets the gender.
"Måste" has no infinitive form – it's always "måste" in all tenses.
"Får" = may/allowed to. "Får inte" = must not / not allowed to.
Kan means both 'can' and 'know how to': Hon kan prata means she knows how to speak.

target: Kan du öppna fönstret under veckan alltid?
english: Can you open the window during the week always?
tip: "Kan du" + infinitive is the standard polite request format.

target: Jag saknar er på morgonen verkligen.
english: I really miss you in the morning.
tip: "Er" is both 'you' (object, plural) and 'your.' Context determines the meaning.

target: Han ska ha sagt att han inte visste.
english: He supposedly said he didn't know.
tip: "Ska ha" + supine = reportedly/supposedly. Distances from the claim.

target: Vi vet inte var han bor med familjen.
english: We don't know where he lives with the family.
tip: After var, the subclause keeps the subject before the verb: var han bor, not var bor han.
Hit means motion to here; static here is här. Kom hit = come toward me, but Jag är här = I am here.
Var is the imperative of vara (to be), an irregular form: Var tyst = be quiet.
Negative commands put inte after the verb: Spring inte = don't run, literally run not.
Swedish uses the definite väskan (the bag) where English says your bag: Packa väskan.
Såg is the irregular past of se (to see); the vowel shifts from e to å: Jag såg henne.
Minns ends in -s but is not passive; minnas is a deponent verb meaning remember: Jag minns henne.
Modal + inte + infinitive: the negation goes between the modal and main verb.
Tänka takes på for think about: Han tänker på henne. Without på it means intend or plan.
Trötta ut is a particle verb meaning wear out; the stress lands on ut: Han tröttade ut mig.
Hem means homeward (motion); at home is hemma. De följde mig hem = they walked me home.
Lära with an object means teach; lära sig means learn: De lärde oss allt = they taught us everything.
Language names are lowercase in Swedish: engelska, never Engelska. Jag kan tala engelska.
Two objects: the person (dem) comes before the thing (vägen), with no preposition: Jag visade dem vägen.
Bad is the irregular past of be (to ask): Hon bad mig vänta = she asked me to wait.
Sin means his or her own and points back to the subject: Hon gav oss sin adress = her own address.

english: She promised me that she would come.
tip: Att is the infinitive marker, like English to: att komma = to come, in Hon lovade mig att komma.
Bjuda på means treat someone to: De bjöd mig på middag = they treated me to dinner.
"Vill ha" = want (a thing). Just "vill" = want (to do). Don't forget "ha" with nouns.
"Låna" means both to borrow and to lend – context determines which.
Swish is Sweden's mobile payment app – used everywhere from stores to street vendors.

target: Det finns en park i närheten.
tip: Det finns means there is or there are for existence: Det finns en park i närheten.

target: Han kan laga mat riktigt bra.
tip: Laga mat means to cook; laga on its own means to repair: Han kan laga mat riktigt bra.
